title: Harmonizer: model-gating and soft-eviction plan for speculative decode
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: implement the 'Harmonizer' runtime component that performs model-gating, soft-eviction, and acceptance scoring for speculative decode flows while coordinating kernel selection and attention optimizations. This ticket covers the design and initial implementation for model routing heuristics, acceptance metric instrumentation, and a tiered fallback strategy.

Context: speculative decoding improves latency by launching cheap/fast decoders in parallel with higher-quality models. To be production-safe we need a runtime mediator that: (1) decides which candidate model(s) to probe given kernel affinity and attention profile, (2) computes an acceptance score early in the decode path, and (3) performs a deterministic, low-overhead fallback/eviction when acceptance thresholds are missed. Harmonizer will live as a thin orchestration layer in the serving runtime, tightly integrated with kernel selection to prefer models whose kernel/quantization path matches the active attention tiling and KV patterns.

Non-goals: this ticket does not change the model catalog UI, billing surfaces, or the end-to-end user API. It also does not implement long-running A/B rollouts; rollout hooks will be added in a follow-up.

Design notes: Harmonizer will use a two-stage decision process: (A) Gate selection stage computes a gating vector from request metadata (prompt prefix length, attention span hint, token budget), live node metrics (GPU temperature, queue latency), and kernel fingerprints (supported kernels and quantization profile). Candidate models are scored for expected latency/cost and compatibility. (B) Acceptance stage runs during prefill and early decode: the fast candidate emits a lightweight acceptance signal (confidence delta metric based on logit stability and prefix alignment) after the prefill KV sync; if acceptance > threshold we commit the cheap candidate, otherwise we soft-evict it and redirect the tail to the fallback model.

Kernel selection tie-ins: gate scoring prefers model variants with kernels that support attention tiling and efficient KV cache transposition for the observed prompt lengths. When available, Harmonizer will bias towards kernels with fused rotary/ALiBi kernels to reduce per-token overhead during early decode.

Attention optimizations: Harmonizer will expose attention-hint annotations on requests to let the scheduler preselect tiling strategies (axis-aligned vs. block-tiling). These hints will be used in kernel-matching heuristics and telemetry to evaluate the real-world benefit of each tiling choice.

Telemetry & safety: acceptance_score, raw_confidence_delta, latency_delta (probe vs fallback), soft_eviction_count, false_accept_rate, kernel_mismatch_rate, and end-to-end P95 will be logged per-request with tagging for model_variant and kernel_id. All signals will feed the console rollout dashboard and automated regression alerts.

Fallback hierarchy: 1) Immediate fallback to pinned high-quality model variant on soft-eviction; 2) If pinned variant is saturated, route to regional-compatible variant; 3) Last-resort: queue and backpressure with informative error. Implement deterministic ordering so operators can reason about behavior.

Open decisions: how to set dynamic acceptance thresholds (static thresholds vs. percentile-based adaptive thresholds), and cost-accounting for speculative probes. We will prototype percentile-based thresholds in telemetry before rolling out auto-adaptation.

Links: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.io/display/RUN/Harmonizer+Design, prototype benchmark: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1_harmonizer_prototype, initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9876
acceptance_criteria: Harmonizer implemented as a modular runtime component that can be enabled per-model-route
Early acceptance signal computed within prefill + first-k decode window with <0.5ms median overhead per request
False-accept rate < 2% on the synthetic eval corpus and <3% on the staging traffic sample
Soft-eviction triggers failover to pinned fallback with correct token continuity and no duplication
Telemetry emitted for acceptance_score, soft_eviction_count, kernel_id, and latency_delta and visible in runtime dashboards
Bench shows end-to-end P95 latency improvement for opportunistic workloads and <5% cost overhead for steady-state workloads
implementation_tasks: Add Harmonizer component and configuration hooks into runtime router
Implement gate scorer that consumes request metadata and kernel fingerprints
Wire lightweight acceptance signal path into prefill and first-k decode stages
Integrate soft-eviction logic and deterministic fallback ordering
Expose attention-hint annotations and kernel preference in request envelope
Add telemetry, dashboards, and automated regression alerts
End-to-end tests and staging rollout with shadow traffic
